Baroness Orczy, Pimpernel and Rosemary.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/baroness-orczy/pimpernel-and-rosemary

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Baroness Orczy, the author, died 1947.

First publication of the text used: 1925 (SE colophon: 'Pimpernel and Rosemary was published in 1925 by Baroness Orczy.')

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the edition's rights statement (quoted below) places the text in the US public domain. The text was first published in 1925, before 1931.
- Country of origin (United Kingdom): the facts do not name the place of first publication, so the country is taken from the author's citizenship, United Kingdom (Wikidata Q234530 also lists Hungarian citizenship; the text is in English), and the text is in English (en-GB). If the first publication was in the United States instead, the US rule settles the origin, because the text was first published before 1931. Copyright in the United Kingdom lasts life plus 70 years after the death of the last surviving person named above. The last to die did so in 1947, so the work entered the public domain there on 1 January 2018.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon: 'Pimpernel and Rosemary was published in 1925 by Baroness Orczy.'
- Wikidata Q234530 (Baroness Orczy), P570 = 1947-11-12.
